services.title: Services
services.subtitle: Each agent is a radio character with its own folder: frequency, mission, voice and dictation. Tune its frequency in the aircraft and that agent answers.
services.about_atc: Air traffic control on its own frequency.
services.about_commander: Orders to units and mission events.

add.title: New agent
add.about_instructor: A voice in the tower that sees what a tower would see and reads the aircraft's manuals. Rename it and change its mission to make it anyone: a mechanic, a supervisor, a briefing officer.
add.about_squad: An infantry group on the ground that you carry: it moves, waits for pickup, boards and leaves your helicopter, pops smoke.
add.about_vehicles: A group of ground vehicles (armour, APCs, trucks): it drives on or off the road in a formation, reports the enemies it sees and attacks on your order. Vehicles with a troop compartment in DCS (BTR-80, MaxxPro...) pick up a squad and drop it where you say.
add.about_artillery: An artillery battery (BM-21, howitzers, mortars): it never sees its targets and fires where it is told. Give it the point yourself (a mission zone, an F10 map mark, or coordinates read from the map: MGRS or latitude and longitude), or ask a unit that sees the target to call for fire on the internal net. It calls "shot" and "rounds complete" and takes corrections (add, drop, left, right).
add.about_ships: A ship or a group of ships: it sails to coordinates, a zone or an F10 map mark at the speed you give in knots (never over land), fires its guns or missiles at a point like the artillery (calls for fire, corrections, queue), engages enemy ships it detects, and switches on a TACAN on request. An aircraft carrier (the Supercarrier too) also gives ICLS, Link 4 and ACLS and turns into the wind for flying. The carrier's deck crew, LSO and air traffic control stay DCS's own.
add.about_wingman: Your wingman: its own AI aircraft group in the Mission Editor (one aircraft, LATE ACTIVATION ticked, on a parking spot or in the air). Start it by radio ("Manolo, start up, we are leaving"): cold or hot on its parking spot, on the runway, or in the air beside you; once airborne it joins you. Then formation, cover, attack, bombing, orbit and return to base. Call it by name or by its number ("Two, cover me"); it knows its own state, fuel, weapons and what it sees.
add.about_controller: An air controller, like an AWACS or a ground control centre: its eyes are the radar groups of the mission you give it (an AWACS, ground radars, ships). Check in with it once airborne with your weapons: it gives you a task that fits, from its board (units on the internal net ask it for air support), and hands you over to that unit on its frequency. It calls bandits closing on you and enemy radars it hears. It never moves its AWACS for you.
add.group_hint_controller: Exactly as its radar group is called in the Mission Editor (e.g. an E-3 group named Magic AWACS). More radar groups can be listed in its agent.json ("controller": "sensors").
add.number_hint: How you call it in your flight (you are 1): it answers to this number (two, 2...) and to its name.
add.group_hint: Exactly as the infantry group is called in the Mission Editor (e.g. Tango). Only infantry in that group.
add.group_hint_wingman: Exactly as its aircraft group is called in the Mission Editor (e.g. Manolo): one aircraft, LATE ACTIVATION ticked.
add.group_hint_vehicles: Exactly as the vehicle group is called in the Mission Editor (e.g. Bison). Only vehicles in that group.
add.group_hint_ships: Exactly as the ship group is called in the Mission Editor (e.g. Mother). Its first ship is the one that carries the aids.
add.group_hint_artillery: Exactly as the artillery group is called in the Mission Editor (e.g. Archer). Only artillery in that group.

agent.subtitle: {role} · {frequency}
agent.name: Name
agent.name_hint: The name is who this agent is: the model knows it ({name} in the mission) and triggers refer to it.
agent.name_fixed: The ATC is fixed: it answers as each airfield's station, with its own name.
agent.aliases_hint: Several agents may share a frequency: start your call with the name of the one you want ("Tango, move to zone 1"), or call all stations and each answers in turn. It also answers to these names, e.g. a callsign: "Tango 1, Green Team". Without a name, the one you last talked with answers.
agent.group_hint: The agent's unit is this group in the mission. Renamed the group in the Mission Editor? Write its new name here too: changing the agent's name above does not change the group.
agent.number_hint: How you call it in your flight (you are 1): it answers to this number and to its name.
agent.group_hint_wingman: The wingman is this aircraft group in the mission (LATE ACTIVATION ticked: it starts when you tell it to). Renamed the group in the Mission Editor? Write its new name here too.
agent.airfield_note: This agent answers on each airfield's own ATC frequency: tune the tower of the airfield you want to talk to.
agent.how_text: The frequency switches the agent on: when the radio you transmit on is tuned to it, this agent hears you and answers on it, with its own mission, voice and dictation. Agents may share a frequency: the one you call by name answers, and all of them hear everything said on it.
agent.how_folder: Everything this agent uses is kept in its own folder: agents/<name>/.
agent.delete_hint: Its folder is kept in backups/agents: move it back to agents/ to restore it.
agent.delete_confirm: Delete {name}? It goes off the air at once.
agent.deleted: {name} deleted. Its folder was kept in {folder}.

memory.chatter: Talks on its own in calm moments
memory.chatter_rare: Now and then (after 15 min of silence)

assistant.title: Triggers assistant
assistant.text: Tell it in your own words, in any language, what should happen in your mission. It fills in this tab's rows; nothing is saved until you press Save triggers.
assistant.placeholder: e.g. When the helicopter enters zone LZ I turn on flag 10: the squad calls me if they see it. When I say I see the smoke, turn on flag 20.
assistant.review: Rows changed (outlined in blue): review them and press Save triggers.
assistant.error_none: No brain is configured: set "brain" in settings.json.
assistant.error_sign_in: The ChatGPT sign-in is missing or expired: run utilities\CHATGPT_LOGIN.cmd.
assistant.error_limit: The plan's usage limit was reached: try again later.

triggers.fixed: The ATC is fixed: it has no triggers. Give triggers to the other agents.
triggers.events_text: The agent calls you on the radio by itself, when a flag turns on or when something happens to a squad (seen by the program itself: nothing to do in the Mission Editor). Write in plain words what it should tell you; it says it in character, from what it can really see, and never invents what it cannot see.
triggers.cond_fuel_low: The wingman is low on fuel (bingo)
triggers.cond_out_of_weapons: The wingman has no weapons left (winchester)
triggers.instructions_example: If you see the helicopter, call the pilot and tell them where you are relative to it.
triggers.actions_text: Each action is a button only this agent can press: when it decides the moment has come (from what you say on the radio and what it sees), it turns the flag on, and your mission's triggers do the rest (or, for an Internal flag, another agent's event).
triggers.when_example: When the pilot says they see your smoke.
triggers.example_intro: Your squad calls you when the helicopter arrives, and the mission moves on when you see their smoke.
triggers.example_1: Mission Editor: a trigger zone LZ and a trigger: TYPE ONCE, condition UNIT INSIDE ZONE (your helicopter, LZ), action FLAG ON (10).
triggers.example_2: Here, an event: flag 10, "If you see the helicopter, call the pilot and tell them where you are relative to it."
triggers.example_3: Here, an action: smoke_ready, turns on flag 20, "When the pilot says they see your smoke."
triggers.example_4: Mission Editor: a trigger: condition FLAG IS TRUE (20), action whatever comes next (a message, AI TASK PUSH, a group activates...).
triggers.example_note: Any flag number or name works: use the same one here and in the Mission Editor, and one your mission does not use for something else.
triggers.internal_hint: An internal flag links agents without the Mission Editor: one agent's action turns it on, another agent's event (same flag, also internal) fires at once, on any frequency. DCS never sees it.
triggers.example_internal: Internal flags, agent to agent: Tango gets an action confirm_in_z1, turns on flag tango_z1, Internal, "When your team is in zone 1." Victor gets an event: flag tango_z1, Internal, "Call the pilot and ask whether we advance." Nothing in the Mission Editor.
triggers.example_condition: Events without flags: Victor gets an event When "Soldiers are killed", "Tell the pilot how many men you lost and ask for support." Or When "The squad is wiped out", Whose squad: Tango, "Tell the pilot Tango is no longer answering." They fire on a change, never for how things are at the start, and at most once a minute.

stt.provider_hint: The same for every agent; chosen in settings.json "speech.provider" for now.
stt.language_hint: The language you speak to this agent in. Each press uses the language of the agent on that frequency.
stt.change_microphone: Change it in Controls and audio
